decision.detail: At six in the lobby, Phil stops at the coat-check counter, pulls his own envelope from the rack—his name, his coach ticket, his return stub—and tucks it inside his jacket. He buttons the jacket. He walks past the coffee urn without stopping. He walks out the front door into the February air, puts his hands in his pockets, and walks the two blocks to the coach terminal. He does not look at the piano through the ballroom glass. He does not stop for the driver with the flat tire. He does not turn back toward the Rialto. He gets on the coach, sits in the aisle seat, and puts his head against the window until the town is a smear of grey and the road is straight and the miles are counting.
decision.intention: Be in Pittsburgh by dark. Be at my sister's door at eight on Wednesday. Lift the couch. The thing is the thing. Nothing else is required of the day.
decision.words: Loudly, to no one in particular, as the door swings shut behind him: "I've got a couch to move on the other side of the river. Don't wait up."
